answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a slashable stake that becomes its anchor of trust. At dawn a newcomer holds no reputation and must earn it through repeated, verifiable trades. To impersonate a thousand peers, an attacker has to lock capital in every fake account, so the cost grows linearly with the Sybil count, and one caught fraud slashes the entire bond. With a raven watching for cheaters, a single exposed lie costs far more than any short-term gain.
